rationale: Log deletion destroys forensic evidence, violates chain of custody, and breaches compliance requirements across PCI-DSS 10.5.1, HIPAA §164.312(b), GDPR Art.5(1)(e), NIST AU-9. Even scheduled deletions require human visibility during an active incident.
pre_execution_requirements: Create backup of logs before deletion
violation_message: 🚨 CRITICAL: Log/audit trail deletion requested. This action destroys forensic evidence, violates chain of custody, and is blocked from auto-execution unconditionally. Requires L2 + Manager approval.
source_reference: PCI-DSS v4 10.5.1 | HIPAA §164.312(b) | NIST 800-53 AU-9 | GDPR Art.5(1)(e)

rationale: Permanent data destruction is irreversible. NIST SP 800-88 Rev.1 mandates a documented destruction process. Execution without verified backup and legal clearance risks compliance violation and permanent evidence loss.
pre_execution_requirements: Verify backups exist and are validated
Obtain legal approval if regulated data involved
Confirm no ongoing legal hold or investigation
Confirm data retention period has expired
violation_message: 🔴 CRITICAL: Permanent/irreversible data destruction requested. This action requires L3 + Director approval and verified backup confirmation before execution.
source_reference: NIST SP 800-88 Rev.1 | GDPR Art.17 | HIPAA §164.310(d)(2) | PCI-DSS v4 9.4.6

rationale: Permanent deletion of infrastructure resources (VMs, databases, images) can cause irrecoverable service loss. Requires backup verification and dependency check before execution.
pre_execution_requirements: Verify recent backup exists and is valid
Document specific resource to be deleted
L2 analyst approves with manager sign-off
violation_message: ⚠️ HIGH RISK: Irrecoverable infrastructure deletion requested. Verify all backups and dependencies before proceeding. Requires L2 + Manager approval.
source_reference: NIST 800-53 CP-9 Information System Backup | ISO 27001 A.8.13 | SOC 2 A1.2

rationale: Network-wide changes affect all users and systems simultaneously. Impact assessment including user count, revenue, and SLA must be done before execution. Only an Incident Commander can authorize.
violation_message: 🚨 CRITICAL: Wide-impact network change proposed. Blast radius is organization-wide. Requires Incident Commander authorization. Impact analysis must be completed first.
source_reference: NIST 800-53 SC-7 / CM-3 | ISO 27001 A.8.20 | SOC 2 A1.1 Availability

rationale: Disabling security controls directly increases attack surface. These actions violate fundamental security operations principles and multiple compliance requirements. Even temporary disabling must be reviewed and logged.
violation_message: 🔒 SECURITY CRITICAL: Disabling a security control increases attack surface and is blocked from auto-execution. Requires L2 + Security Manager approval with documented justification and duration.
source_reference: PCI-DSS v4 8.3.10 | CIS Controls v8 6.5 | ISO 27001:2022 A.8.21 | NIST 800-53 SI-3 / AU-12

rationale: Admin access grants are high-risk and must comply with least-privilege principles. Time-limited JIT access should be preferred over standing admin rights. IAM team review is mandatory to prevent privilege creep.
justification_required: Can this be done with less privilege?
violation_message: 🔑 PRIVILEGE ESCALATION: Admin/root access grant requested. Violates least-privilege principle. Requires IAM team review. Prefer JIT access with max 8h duration.
source_reference: NIST 800-53 AC-6 Least Privilege | CIS Controls v8 5.3 / 6.8 | PCI-DSS v4 7.2 | ISO 27001 A.8.2

rationale: Production changes must go through change management to prevent unintended outages and ensure rollback plans exist. Emergency exceptions (active incident) require Incident Commander authorization and post-incident review.
violation_message: ⚙️ PRODUCTION CHANGE: Change to production environment requires change management approval and a documented rollback plan. Emergency changes require Incident Commander authorization.
source_reference: ITIL Change Management | NIST 800-53 CM-3 Configuration Change Control | ISO 27001 A.8.32 | SOC 2 CC8.1
